RESEARCH / 01

Two constraints.
One physical world.

My MPhil research asks how to learn from imperfect simulations and how to choose the few measurements that matter most. Both questions start with the same reality: field data is scarce, noisy, and expensive to collect.

01SIMULATION → FIELD

TRANSFER LEARNING · INTERPRETABILITY

Learning across the
reality gap.

Numerical models make labeled pressure transients plentiful; real leak records do not. I pre-trained leak-diagnostic models on simulated signals, adapted them with limited experimental data, and used Integrated Gradients to inspect which sensor–time regions informed their predictions.

The attribution analysis surfaced physically meaningful later-time, multiply scattered wave information rather than treating the network as a black box.

02SPARSE OBSERVATION

CONTRASTIVE LEARNING · SENSOR SELECTION

Learning where
to listen.

When only a few sensors can be deployed, placement becomes part of the learning problem. My Deep Contrastive Sensor Selection framework combines supervised contrastive learning with differentiable Top‑K gating to select sensor subsets for the diagnostic task itself.

The Q‑Leak study compares task-aligned selection with a mutual-information-motivated baseline across sensing budgets and noise levels—while noting that the baseline remains competitive in the hardest low-budget settings.

SIDE PROJECT / 04

A better way
to read the evidence.

EvidenceGraph is my research-paper reading project. It helps turn a PDF into an explorable set of passages and relationships, so a question can lead back to the source rather than ending at an answer.

It is a live prototype for more inspectable scientific reading—not a substitute for checking the paper yourself.
